entries.overview: A tough, sickle-shaped vertical sheet of dura mater dipping along the midline crease inside the skull.
entries.function: Separates the left and right cerebral hemispheres and prevents the brain from shifting side to side.

facts: Houses both the superior sagittal sinus along its top rim and the inferior sagittal sinus along its lower edge.
Anchors to the skull in front near the nose bridge and blends behind with the tentorium cerebelli.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Central Nervous System

entries.overview: The crystal-clear domed window covering the front colored iris and pupil of the eyeball.
entries.function: Bends incoming light rays sharply inward toward the lens and shields the front of the eye from dust and germs.

facts: Provides roughly two-thirds of the eye’s total focusing power.
Contains no blood vessels so it stays transparent, receiving oxygen directly from tears and the air.
Heavily supplied with sensory nerve endings that trigger protective blinking when touched.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Vision and Sensory Perception

entries.overview: The ultra-thin light-sensitive neural membrane lining the inside back wall of the eyeball.
entries.function: Converts focused patterns of light into electrical nerve signals sent down the optic nerve to the brain.

facts: Contains rod cells for dim-light vision and cone cells for sharp color vision.
Its central pit, the fovea, provides our crispest reading and face-recognition detail.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Vision and Sensory Perception

entries.overview: A tough, tubular outer sleeve of fibrous connective tissue enclosing the spinal cord inside the vertebral canal.
entries.function: Protects the delicate spinal cord and nerve roots while containing the cushion of cerebrospinal fluid.

facts: Separated from the bony vertebrae by the fat- and vessel-filled epidural space.
Extends downward past the end of the spinal cord down to the sacrum.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Central Nervous System

entries.overview: The thickest, longest nerve in the human body, running from the lower spine deep through the buttock down the leg.
entries.function: Carries movement commands to the hamstrings and lower-leg muscles while returning sensation from most of the leg and foot.

facts: Formed by nerve roots L4 through S3 and emerges below or near the piriformis muscle in the buttock.
Splits above the back of the knee into the tibial nerve and common fibular nerve.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Peripheral Nervous System

entries.overview: A major peripheral nerve descending down the midline of the arm and forearm into the palm.
entries.function: Controls most forearm wrist-flexor and thumb-pinch muscles and supplies touch sensation to the thumb and index fingers.

facts: Passes through the tight carpal tunnel at the wrist beneath a fibrous ligament.
Gives sensation to the palmar side of the thumb, index, middle, and half of the ring finger.
